children: Intel
shares have risen 46% over the past 30 days, with the stock's price approaching its 52-week high of $142.35.
We asked Seeking Alpha analysts
, and
if they thought Intel
was a buy, hold, or sell at these prices.
Julia Ostian: Intel
is currently a Hold because its valuation is seriously stretched.

In my recent overview of the stock, I showed that the current valuation asks for four years of flawless profit growth until 2029 just to trade at a normal industry multiple. At the same time, the business is still burning billions of dollars in free cash flow and absorbing heavy losses in its foundry division while trading way higher than direct peers with way lower valuations.

Because the underlying fundamentals do not yet justify this price, the stock's rally is being driven almost entirely by investor excitement around AI and potential partnerships. The stock may continue rallying, but it should correct once the sentiment cools off.
Danil Sereda: I believe Intel stock remains a Buy even amid the seemingly high forward valuation multiples.

As I wrote in my article, there's a great chance that we'll see INTC's bottom line inflecting above today's base consensus because the firm has only recently come out of a non-GAAP loss and the base for future comparison is still low. In such cases, there's usually a solid consensus-beating potential, in my view. We can recall the way SoFi Technologies
or Palantir
behaved in a similar setup one to two years after breaking even on the bottom line.
Intel's

latest earnings print has proven that Wall Street analysts are still underestimating the true potential. There are plenty of catalysts for Intel to monetize and lean on to be ahead of consensus. We can take its potential profits from the SK hynix
partnership or the recent news that it signed Tesla
and SpaceX
for their xAI division's terafab, which is going to utilize Intel's 14A node.
Of course, CPU usage is growing massively, too, and it appears to be quite early to tell how it's going to impact the bottom line. When GPUs were as hot a topic as CPUs are today, Nvidia
was able to outperform massively, remaining quite expensively valued along the way.
So, with all that being said, I think it's better to keep a Buy rating on INTC for the rest of the year, at least.
(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)
Sharon McArd: I rate Intel a Buy. The recently reported SK hynix

discussions are another potential catalyst, but they’re not the main reason I’m constructive. My thesis is that Intel’s execution, better data center performance, and Foundry progress are all changing the long-term outlook gradually. Execution risks still remain, particularly around turning Foundry into a consistently profitable business, but I still think the risk/reward is attractive for patient investors.
For those looking at the AI semiconductor ecosystem, overall I remain constructive on Advanced Micro Devices
, Nvidia
, and SK hynix
, although for me, Intel
has a different turnaround profile than those companies.
